# Workflows

- `rust.yml` (Rust): on every pull request and push to main, runs `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo deny check`, the chart checks (`cargo xtask crdgen --check` and `cargo xtask helm-test`), and an image build that does not push.
- `action.yml` (Action): on pushes to main and on pull requests that touch `action/` or `docs/ci/`, tests the JavaScript GitHub Action (including `action/action.yml` as YAML) and runs shellcheck on `docs/ci/buildkit-allocate.sh`.
- `e2e.yml` (E2E): on every pull request and push to main, the end-to-end suite (`cargo xtask e2e`), the cheap kind suites (`crd-verify`, `render-verify`, `helm-verify`), a dry run of `examples/` against the CRDs on a kind cluster, and the real Action job with the job's OIDC token (same-repository pull requests only, `id-token: write`). Nightly and on demand, it runs the other kind suites (`alloc-verify`, `api-verify`, `runtime-verify`, `reconcile-verify`, `edge-verify`, `claim-verify`, `proxy-verify`), the drain suite and the certificate soak. Each kind job has its own runner, so none sets `BK_KIND_SUFFIX`.
- `audit.yml` (Audit): nightly `cargo deny check advisories`, so a new RUSTSEC advisory shows up without a code change.
- `docs.yml` (Docs): builds the documentation site (`cargo xtask docs`) on every pull request, which also catches broken links, and deploys it to GitHub Pages from main.
- `release.yml` (Release): on `vX.Y.Z` tags. A gate job requires the tag commit to be on main with green Rust and Action push runs. Builds linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 natively, pushes the multi-arch index by digest, signs it and the per-arch manifests with cosign (keyless), attaches an SPDX SBOM that lists the Rust crates (built with `cargo auditable`) and SLSA provenance, scans the unsigned digest with a checksum-pinned Trivy binary in a job with read-only package access, signs only after the scan passes, and only then adds the version and `sha-` tags, packages the Helm chart onto the GitHub release, and moves the `vN` tag that the GitHub Action is published under, only when the new tag is the highest stable version in its major.

Release notes are the notes GitHub generates from merged pull requests. No workflow needs a repository secret beyond the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Every third-party action is pinned to a full commit SHA with its version in a comment, and Renovate keeps the pins current (see [RENOVATE.md](../RENOVATE.md)).
